public_rationale: Only the firm clause, that generative AI is deeply unprofitable, is scored. The productivity and customer-loss clauses are hedged ('doesn't seem to', 'appears to'). For the period before the April 2026 post, Anthropic's S-1 shows deep operating losses: $2.1 billion in the first half of 2025, on full-year 2025 revenue of about $4.6 billion. Q1 2026 was also a loss of about $1.67 billion on $4.73 billion of revenue. The filing says the June 2026 quarter was its first operating profit in any reported period. So one of the two leading generative AI labs was deeply unprofitable when he wrote. The picture shifted soon after: Anthropic made an operating profit in Q2 2026 and an adjusted profit for the first half. That is after the post and does not change the finding for the period described.
limitations: Only one company's results are cited for an industry-wide claim.
The hedged clauses are not graded.
The S-1 figures come through news and analyst summaries, because the SEC page was not readable.

our_interpretation: Only the unhedged clause, 'generative AI is deeply unprofitable', is scored. The other two clauses are hedged with 'doesn't seem to' and 'appears to'. They are his impressions, not firm claims, so they are not scored.

Plain reading of the scored clause: the companies that build and sell generative AI models and services were losing large sums relative to their revenue. In context he is talking about OpenAI, Anthropic, and AI startups.

He named no period. I use the latest periods public data could cover before the April 21, 2026 post: calendar 2025 (he cites 'last year' revenues) through the March 2026 quarter. This is my choice and is flagged.
I read 'deeply' as losses that are large relative to revenue, not small or near breakeven.
criteria.support_condition: Company-reported results for leading generative AI developers show operating losses that are large relative to revenue in 2025 through Q1 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Company-reported results show leading generative AI developers were profitable or near breakeven in 2025 through Q1 2026.
